sections.overview: This resident woodpecker ranges across South and Southeast Asia.
sections.identification: It is 28–30 cm long; males have a red crown and both sexes a golden-red back.
sections.habitat: It uses open and secondary woodland, forest edges, plantations and parks, and can also occur in mangroves and cultivated landscapes.
sections.diet: It searches tree trunks, palms and other vegetation for insects, and accounts also describe it catching insects in flight.
sections.behavior: Like other woodpeckers, it climbs trunks with its strong feet and tail support; it is generally resident rather than a long-distance migrant.
sections.reproduction: It is a resident breeder in Singapore, but the concise regional accounts consulted do not establish one breeding calendar for its broad Asian range.
sections.ecology: Six subspecies are recognized; Everett’s Flameback (D. everetti) was formerly included here.
sections.conservation: Oiseaux.net lists it globally as Least Concern.
